findings: All eighteen stages were attempted and terminal; four selected models were independently graded, all accepted. These are the same two asymmetric-interaction cases in NYX-requested search and fixed control, not four independent task successes. Four of six tasks per search arm remain ungraded; the model-authored arm submitted none. This is not a complete score.

NYX-requested search admitted a competing population on first generation for three cases and after a second generation on two more. Its two accepted cases both required repair of undersized support limits. The fixed control admitted first-generation populations on all six and solved the same two without inference. No fresh cognitive advantage or matched-realized-compute claim is established.

Twelve real registered R3B observations were executed, with source integrity, sandbox cleanup and temporary fixture removal verified. All four fixed-control populations in the other two families were refuted by the prospective observation; no hidden grade fed repair or selection.

Thirteen of fifteen admitted NYX-search fits had rank four for four calibration rows; two had rank three. This exposes data-saturated interpolation in the candidate population. Every successful fixed search stopped at three models after 28 supports. The hypothesis that early saturated fits displace lower-complexity hypotheses needs general development testing, not tuning on this exposed corpus.

Exact rejected structures are unavailable. NYX recorded four candidate-limit outcomes at 10,8,6,10 supports and five model-limit outcomes; two successful cases required the second call. No native budget exhaustion occurred.
